title: Why are we all so stressed?
reason: 上一课聚焦科技模型与数据判断，今天轮换到工作生活平衡和压力管理。本集讨论时间不足、长期过载、过劳以及不同人的应对方法，适合联系平台故障处理、项目交付和团队管理中的真实压力。练习反复调用应对压力、因果关系、适度标准和避免一刀切方案的高频表达，帮助学习者从理解逐步过渡到用简洁英语说明自己的工作方法。

targetExpressions.meaning: manage difficult situations that cause worry or pressure
targetExpressions.usage: Use cope with before the source of stress: She pauses to cope with stressful situations at work.

targetExpressions.meaning: cause physical or mental exhaustion after too much work or stress
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to show a possible result: Constant overtime can lead to burnout.
Use it when pressure or an activity improves focus: A short deadline can sometimes sharpen the mind.

targetExpressions.expression: good enough rather than always trying for perfection
targetExpressions.meaning: accept a satisfactory result instead of demanding a perfect one every time
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to describe a practical standard: For a first draft, aim for good enough rather than always trying for perfection.

targetExpressions.meaning: when discussing or dealing with a particular subject
targetExpressions.usage: Follow it with a noun or -ing form: When it comes to incident reviews, clear facts matter most.

targetExpressions.meaning: using the same solution for everyone instead of considering different needs
targetExpressions.usage: Use it before a noun or after be: A one-size-fits-all approach rarely works for team productivity.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Becca's question to Neil: How do you ______?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Becca asks how Neil manages pressure using the exact phrase “cope with stressful situations”.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What may happen if feeling overwhelmed becomes long-term chronic stress?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Claudia says temporary overwhelm can become chronic stress, which might lead to burnout.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the programme's positive point: Before an exam, nerves may ______ and help you do your best.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript says nerves can sharpen thinking or concentrate the mind, allowing someone to perform well.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence best matches Claudia's advice for reducing stress?
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: good enough rather than always trying for perfection

options.text: Accept that some work can be good enough rather than always trying for perfection.
Refuse to finish any task until every detail is perfect.
Add more items to the to-do list whenever you feel stressed.
Assume that stress management works identically for everyone.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Claudia recommends slowing down and accepting “good enough” instead of always aiming for perfection.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the topic phrase: There is no single best answer ______ managing stress.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Iqra uses “when it comes to this” to focus the discussion on ways of dealing with overwhelm.

options.text: The same solution is applied to different people or problems.
Each person's needs are considered separately.
Every difficult task is removed permanently.
Only one item is placed on a to-do list.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme defines “one-size-fits-all” as applying the same solution to many different problems instead of treating them individually.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the work sentence with today's expression: Repeated overnight incident calls without recovery time can ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: “Lead to burnout” naturally expresses the possible result of continuing overload, following the episode's cause-and-effect explanation.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why does Claudia say people should not worry too much about reaching the end of their to-do list?
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: good enough rather than always trying for perfection

options.text: New tasks will appear, so accepting a reasonable stopping point can be healthier.
A busy life contains no tasks that need to be completed.
Every to-do list automatically disappears overnight.
Working without rest is the most effective stress technique.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Claudia says a to-do list never truly ends because something new will appear tomorrow; this supports accepting “good enough” rather than perfection.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) problem—what overwhelm and chronic stress can cause; (2) two ideas—how nerves can sometimes help and why perfection creates pressure; (3) advice—why people need different ways to manage stress. Phrase bank: “lead to burnout”, “sharpen the mind”, “one-size-fits-all”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough.
referencePoints: Neil feels stressed when he lacks time; Becca feels stressed when doing something new that she has not mastered.
Overwhelm may be temporary, but chronic stress can lead to burnout, meaning mental or physical exhaustion from overwork.
Nerves before an exam or performance can sharpen thinking and may help someone perform better.
Slowing down and accepting “good enough” rather than always seeking perfection can reduce stress.
There is no one-size-fits-all solution because different people and problems may need different approaches.
A to-do list never truly ends; reading for pleasure was identified as the most restful activity in the research discussed.
